headline: Democratic senators demand Pentagon reveal 'true cost' of Iran war
dek: Democratic senators wrote the Pentagon demanding disclosure of the Iran war's true cost, citing the Pentagon's own watchdog: US service members killed (ByteSEU live update relays CENTCOM figure of 18) and 865 injured since the conflict began; US bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, UAE, Saudi Arabia,…
sources: USA Today (Oct 19, ~17:00 ; senators' letter quoting Pentagon Inspector-General-style watchdog report); Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao (interview) on Bahrain damage
fault_line: War bill: is withholding the rebuild cost estimate prudent planning — or is the public being kept from the real price of the Iran war?

sections.what_happened: Democratic senators wrote the Pentagon demanding disclosure of the Iran war's true cost, citing the Pentagon's own watchdog: US service members killed (ByteSEU live update relays CENTCOM figure of 18) and 865 injured since the conflict began; US bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Oman and Jordan damaged or destroyed by Iranian strikes; Naval Support Activity Bahrain — the US Navy's main Middle East logistics hub — 'severely damaged' by an Iranian missile/drone attack at the war's start; Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao confirmed Iran 'blew the hell out of Bahrain'; damage complicated resupply of the USS Abraham Lincoln. Military justifies withholding cost estimates: undecided which bases it will rebuild. Senators: 'There is no rationale for classifying that cost estimate.'
sections.what_verified: Senators' letter text (USA Today); on-the-record Cao quote; watchdog report exists per letter. CENTCOM 18-KIA figure via ByteSEU live update — single relay, treat as partially supported.
sections.what_disputed: The Pentagon's position is not a cover-up by definition: it says estimates depend on rebuild decisions; senators dispute that rationale.
sections.why_matters: Pocketbook angle first: senators say the Pentagon won't tell America what the Iran war cost — while a watchdog report says bases across EIGHT countries were damaged or destroyed and Bahrain was 'blown the hell' up. The fight over the bill is now the story.
sections.context: Background: Democratic senators demand Pentagon reveal 'true cost' of Iran war — Pentagon watchdog report: 865 injured, bases damaged across 8 countries, Bahrain hub 'severely damaged'

totw_analysis: Our read: Pocketbook angle first: senators say the Pentagon won't tell America what the Iran war cost — while a watchdog report says bases across EIGHT countries were damaged or destroyed and Bahrain was 'blown the hell' up. The fight over the bill is now the story. The fault line our audience is arguing over: War bill: is withholding the rebuild cost estimate prudent planning — or is the public being kept from the real price of the Iran war?
